data.title: Open Redirect
data.summary: The application redirected to a destination taken from the request without validating it, so a link on the organisation's own domain could send a visitor to an attacker's site. The value of the finding is the credibility the domain lends to phishing.
data.description:
Redirect parameters exist for good reasons — returning a user to where they were after login — and become a finding when the destination is not constrained.

The impact is mostly in what the link enables. A URL beginning with the organisation's real domain, with a valid certificate, passes the inspection users are trained to perform and survives many link filters, before delivering them to a credential-harvesting page. In a red team engagement this materially raises phishing success rates.

Open redirects also weaken OAuth and SSO flows, where a redirect chain can carry a token to an unintended destination, and provide a bypass step for SSRF allow-lists that permit the first hop.
data.recommendation:
* Validate the destination against an allow-list of paths or hosts.
* Prefer relative paths, or map an identifier to a known destination server-side.
* Where an external destination is legitimate, show an interstitial naming the destination.
* Register exact redirect URIs with the identity provider and refuse wildcards.
data.short_recommendation: Allow-list redirect destinations rather than reflecting them.
